answer: The joiner fits his staves edge to edge, and the fit must be so close no light shows through the joint. Cooper chestnut stave jointer hoop bond rules the joining: a bond chestnut stave jointers lodge after jointing bench trials. First comes the signal, fitted at dawn; then the summit, fitted before the barrel is raised; the haven is the barrel itself, tight as a drum. To fake it, a cheat must fit 17 false joints and raise 17 false barrels.
